skill.name: research
skill.description: Answer a question with a written report from the live web, where each cited sentence links to a page read in that run. Use it when someone wants an answer with its sources, not a table of rows. A report costs $0.10, $0.30 or $1.00 and starts only after the person approves that price.
skill.summary: Get a live web research report with numbered source citations after approving the price.
skill.author: specstream

security_audit.summary: The ten shell execution alerts match Markdown inline formatting, and the documentation URL is a passive reference. The configured SpecStream endpoint receives research questions after price approval, but the skill does not require consent to share the exact text. No evidence of malicious intent or prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Price approval does not explicitly authorize sharing the question
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact question and name SpecStream before submission. Ask the user to remove sensitive details and approve both the text transfer and the price.

content.user_title: Research Questions With Cited Web Reports
content.value_statement: A web search can leave you comparing pages without a clear answer. This skill turns live web sources into a written report with numbered citations.
actual_capabilities: Shows prices for quick, standard, and deep reports before starting paid work.
Breaks a question into parts, searches the live web, and returns a Markdown report with numbered links to pages read.
Sets the report length and output language independently of research depth.
Limits or excludes source domains for a report.
Requests structured output using a supplied JSON Schema.
Checks run status, cancels a run, or lists previous reports for the account.
limitations: Requires a configured SpecStream MCP connector and browser sign-in on first use.
Sends the research question to SpecStream, so do not include confidential details.
Requires a new price approval for each report, including a repeat at a different depth.
Produces research reports rather than comparable rows or instant single-fact answers.

use_cases.title: Compare vendor documentation
use_cases.description: Compare public release notes and feature documentation before adding tools to an evaluation list.

use_cases.title: Prepare a sourced briefing
use_cases.description: Summarize public agency guidance for a briefing and keep the original source links available for verification.

use_cases.title: Review language changes
use_cases.description: Summarize official release notes for a programming language update before planning a migration.

prompt_templates.title: Ask one research question
prompt_templates.prompt: What are the tradeoffs between heat pumps and gas furnaces in cold climates? Quote the quick report price and wait for my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Compare public guidance
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Compare sources with a defined scope.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare EPA and CDC guidance on indoor air quality during wildfire smoke. Suggest a research depth, quote the price, and wait for approval.

prompt_templates.title: Limit sources and set the language
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Control source domains and report format.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how web browsers handle third-party cookies using only developer.mozilla.org and web.dev. Write a short report in Spanish. Quote the standard price and wait.

prompt_templates.title: Request structured research output
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Supply a JSON Schema for downstream review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare municipal heat action plans using only official city websites. Use my attached JSON Schema. Keep source links where the schema allows. Quote the deep report price and wait for approval.

output_examples.input: Price a quick report on heat pumps in cold climates.
output_examples.output: A quick report costs $0.10. Do you approve this price?

output_examples.input: I approve the $0.10 quick report. Research Python 3.12 changes using only docs.python.org.
output_examples.output:
Python 3.12 introduced a new syntax for type parameters [1]. It also removed the distutils module from the standard library [1].

[1] Python 3.12 release notes: https://docs.python.org/3.12/whatsnew/3.12.html

best_practices: State one clear research question and name any domains to include or exclude.
Review the exact question before approving a report, and remove private details.
Open the cited pages to verify claims before relying on the report.
anti_patterns: Include credentials, customer data, or internal documents in a research question.
Assume an account balance gives permission to start or repeat paid work.
Use a paid report for a single fact that a quick web lookup can answer.

faq.question: What does a report cost?
faq.answer: The skill lists $0.10 for quick, $0.30 for standard, and $1.00 for deep. It checks the price before asking for approval.

faq.question: How long does a report take?
faq.answer: A quick report takes about a minute. A deeper report can take several minutes.

faq.question: Can I choose the sources?
faq.answer: You can specify domains to include or exclude. Each numbered citation links to a page read for that report.

faq.question: Can I get structured output instead of Markdown?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a JSON Schema that describes the output you need.

faq.question: Where does my research question go?
faq.answer: The skill sends the question to the configured SpecStream service. Remove any sensitive details before approving a run.

faq.question: When am I charged?
faq.answer: The skill says a report is charged once on delivery. Failed or cancelled runs are not charged.
